metadata.name: WordPress Core Execution Tests - Rewrite and Permalinks
metadata.description: Code generation tasks for WordPress Rewrite and Permalinks APIs

tests.prompt: Implement a function that registers item URLs under items/<item-slug> as an extra permalink structure using a %wpbp_item% placeholder.
tests.expected_behavior: Reviewer contract: The helper must register the %wpbp_item% rewrite tag, expose the wpbp_item query variable, and add a wpbp_item permastruct whose structure contains items/%wpbp_item%. Review focus: Use WordPress rewrite APIs and do not flush rewrite rules during normal runtime. The runtime inspects WordPress rewrite state after calling the helper rather than trusting its return value.
requirements: Avoid flushing rewrite rules during normal runtime

required_patterns.description: Registers the requested item permalink structure

forbidden_patterns.description: Does not flush rewrite rules during normal runtime
Does not flush rewrite rules during normal runtime

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_rewrite_permalinks_001' ) ) { return false; } global $wp, $wp_rewrite; wpbp_rewrite_permalinks_001(); $tag_index = array_search( '%wpbp_item%', $wp_rewrite->rewritecode, true ); if ( false === $tag_index ) { return false; } $regex = $wp_rewrite->rewritereplace[ $tag_index ] ?? ''; $pattern = '~^' . str_replace( '~', '\\~', $regex ) . '$~'; $accepts_slug = 1 === @preg_match( $pattern, 'alpha-1' ); $rejects_nested_path = 1 !== @preg_match( $pattern, 'alpha/beta' ); $query_replace = $wp_rewrite->queryreplace[ $tag_index ] ?? ''; $struct = $wp_rewrite->extra_permastructs['wpbp_item']['struct'] ?? ''; return $accepts_slug && $rejects_nested_path && 'wpbp_item=' === $query_replace && in_array( 'wpbp_item', $wp->public_query_vars, true ) && str_contains( $struct, 'items/%wpbp_item%' );
assertions.description: The helper registers the item rewrite tag, query var, and permastruct in WordPress

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_rewrite_permalinks_001(): void { add_rewrite_tag( '%wpbp_item%', '([^/]+)' ); add_permastruct( 'wpbp_item', 'items/%wpbp_item%', array( 'with_front' => false ) ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that registers a top-priority rewrite rule for URLs like wpbp-rule/<code>, mapping the captured code to the wpbp_rule query variable.
tests.expected_behavior: Reviewer contract: The helper must add a rewrite rule to WordPress' top rewrite-rule bucket for wpbp-rule/<code> URLs and map the first path segment to the wpbp_rule query variable. Review focus: Use the Rewrite API, use top priority, and do not flush rewrite rules during normal runtime. The runtime inspects $wp_rewrite->extra_rules_top after calling the helper.
requirements: Register the rule at top priority
Avoid flushing rewrite rules during normal runtime

required_patterns.description: Maps to the requested query variable
Adds the rule at top priority
Uses the first regex capture in the query mapping

forbidden_patterns.description: Does not flush rewrite rules during normal runtime
Does not flush rewrite rules during normal runtime

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_rewrite_permalinks_002' ) ) { return false; } global $wp_rewrite; wpbp_rewrite_permalinks_002(); foreach ( $wp_rewrite->extra_rules_top as $regex => $query ) { $pattern = '~' . str_replace( '~', '\\~', $regex ) . '~'; if ( 1 !== @preg_match( $pattern, 'wpbp-rule/abc-123' ) ) { continue; } if ( is_array( $query ) ) { if ( isset( $query['wpbp_rule'] ) && '$matches[1]' === $query['wpbp_rule'] ) { return true; } continue; } if ( is_string( $query ) && str_contains( $query, 'wpbp_rule=$matches[1]' ) ) { return true; } } return false;

tests.prompt: Implement a function that makes wpbp_var available as a public query variable without removing existing public query vars.
tests.expected_behavior: Reviewer contract: The helper must hook query_vars, append wpbp_var, and preserve the incoming public query vars array. Review focus: Use WordPress hook/query-var APIs and do not flush rewrite rules during normal runtime. The runtime applies the filter to a seed array and verifies both the new and existing vars remain present.
requirements: Avoid flushing rewrite rules during normal runtime

required_patterns.description: Adds the requested public query var

forbidden_patterns.description: Does not flush rewrite rules during normal runtime
Does not flush rewrite rules during normal runtime

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_rewrite_permalinks_003' ) ) { return false; } wpbp_rewrite_permalinks_003(); $vars = apply_filters( 'query_vars', array( 'p', 'page_id' ) ); return in_array( 'wpbp_var', $vars, true ) && in_array( 'p', $vars, true ) && in_array( 'page_id', $vars, true ) && 1 === count( array_keys( $vars, 'wpbp_var', true ) );

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_rewrite_permalinks_003(): void { add_filter( 'query_vars', fn( $vars ) => array_merge( $vars, array( 'wpbp_var' ) ) ); }

tests.prompt: Give every single post a reviews view reachable by appending wpbp-reviews to its permalink, exposed to the site as the wpbp-reviews query variable. The suffix may carry a value, and it may also be used bare with nothing after it: WordPress hands a bare endpoint through as an empty string, but the site must see the value 'all' in that case. A value that is present must reach the site unchanged, and requests that do not use the suffix at all must not gain the variable. Do not flush the rewrite rules.
tests.expected_behavior: Reviewer contract: an endpoint is added to the permalink rewrite rules (which also registers the query variable), and the parsed request variables are adjusted so that a present-but-empty endpoint value becomes 'all' by the time the site reads them - either through the `request` filter or on the `parse_request` action, both of which run before the query is built. Review focus: the endpoint mask must cover single post permalinks, the adjustment must distinguish 'key present and empty' from 'key absent', and re-initialising the rewrite object would discard the endpoint. Runtime validation inspects the generated rules and resolves three different variable sets through both hooks.
requirements: Add the endpoint to single post permalinks and expose wpbp-reviews as a query variable
Turn a present but empty endpoint value into 'all' while leaving a supplied value alone
Leave requests that never used the endpoint untouched
Add the endpoint as this code loads: WordPress has already fired init, so deferring it to that action would never run

required_patterns.description: Attaches the endpoint to post permalinks

forbidden_patterns.description: Does not flush rewrite rules during normal runtime
Does not flush rewrite rules during normal runtime

assertions.code: global $wp, $wp_rewrite; $query_vars = apply_filters( 'query_vars', $wp->public_query_vars ); if ( ! in_array( 'wpbp-reviews', $query_vars, true ) ) { return false; } $rules = $wp_rewrite->wp_rewrite_rules(); $has_rule = false; foreach ( $rules as $regex => $query ) { if ( ! is_string( $query ) || ! str_contains( $query, 'wpbp-reviews=' ) ) { continue; } if ( 1 === preg_match( '#^' . $regex . '#', 'hello-world/wpbp-reviews/newest/' ) ) { $has_rule = true; break; } } if ( ! $has_rule ) { return false; } $resolve = static function ( array $query_vars ): array { $query_vars = (array) apply_filters( 'request', $query_vars ); $env = new WP(); $env->query_vars = $query_vars; do_action_ref_array( 'parse_request', array( &$env ) ); return (array) $env->query_vars; }; $empty = $resolve( array( 'name' => 'hello-world', 'wpbp-reviews' => '' ) ); if ( 'all' !== ( $empty['wpbp-reviews'] ?? null ) ) { return false; } if ( 'hello-world' !== ( $empty['name'] ?? null ) ) { return false; } $valued = $resolve( array( 'name' => 'hello-world', 'wpbp-reviews' => 'newest' ) ); if ( 'newest' !== ( $valued['wpbp-reviews'] ?? null ) ) { return false; } $absent = $resolve( array( 'name' => 'hello-world' ) ); return ! array_key_exists( 'wpbp-reviews', $absent ) && 'hello-world' === ( $absent['name'] ?? null );
assertions.description: The endpoint rule and query variable exist and only a present-but-empty value is promoted for the site

exploit_solutions:
add_rewrite_endpoint( 'wpbp-reviews', EP_PERMALINK );
add_filter( 'request', static function ( array $query_vars ): array { $query_vars['wpbp-reviews'] = $query_vars['wpbp-reviews'] ?: 'all'; return $query_vars; } );

add_rewrite_endpoint( 'wpbp-reviews', EP_PERMALINK );
add_filter( 'request', static function ( array $query_vars ): array { if ( empty( $query_vars['wpbp-reviews'] ) ) { return $query_vars; } return $query_vars; } );

tests.prompt: This site publishes posts under /blog/<post-name>/. Provide a routine that registers a public content type wpbp_guide, labelled 'WPBP Guides', whose entries are addressed directly at /guides/<entry-name>/ — the blog prefix that WordPress puts in front of permalink structures must not appear in them — and whose URLs WordPress can resolve back to the entry. Do not flush the rewrite rules.
tests.expected_behavior: Reviewer contract: the post type is registered publicly with a rewrite configuration that sets the base to 'guides' and opts out of the permalink front, so its permastruct is independent of the /blog/ front used by posts. Review focus: the default rewrite configuration inherits the front, producing /blog/guides/..., and turning rewriting off entirely leaves plain query-string URLs. Runtime validation compares an entry's permalink with an ordinary post's permalink and resolves both URLs back to their IDs.
requirements: Register wpbp_guide as a public content type
Base its permalinks on 'guides' without the permalink front
Keep the entry resolvable from its permalink

required_patterns.description: Uses the requested content type name
Opts out of the permalink front

forbidden_patterns.description: Does not flush rewrite rules during normal runtime
Does not flush rewrite rules during normal runtime

assertions.code: wpbp_rewrite_permalinks_005(); global $wp_rewrite; if ( ! post_type_exists( 'wpbp_guide' ) ) { return false; } $wp_rewrite->wp_rewrite_rules(); $guide_id = wp_insert_post( array( 'post_type' => 'wpbp_guide', 'post_status' => 'publish', 'post_title' => 'WPBP Sample Guide', 'post_name' => 'sample-guide' ) ); $post_id = wp_insert_post( array( 'post_type' => 'post', 'post_status' => 'publish', 'post_title' => 'WPBP Sample Post', 'post_name' => 'sample-post' ) ); $GLOBALS['wpbp_rw_005_posts'] = array( $guide_id, $post_id ); $guide_link = (string) get_permalink( $guide_id ); $post_link = (string) get_permalink( $post_id ); if ( home_url( '/guides/sample-guide/' ) !== $guide_link ) { return false; } if ( home_url( '/blog/sample-post/' ) !== $post_link ) { return false; } if ( $guide_id !== url_to_postid( $guide_link ) ) { return false; } return $post_id === url_to_postid( $post_link );
assertions.description: Guide permalinks skip the blog front, ordinary posts keep it, and both resolve back to their entries

runtime_checks.teardown: foreach ( (array) ( $GLOBALS['wpbp_rw_005_posts'] ?? array() ) as $post_id ) { if ( $post_id ) { wp_delete_post( $post_id, true ); } } if ( post_type_exists( 'wpbp_guide' ) ) { unregister_post_type( 'wpbp_guide' ); } update_option( 'permalink_structure', (string) ( $GLOBALS['wpbp_rw_005_permalink'] ?? '' ) ); $GLOBALS['wp_rewrite']->init(); delete_option( 'rewrite_rules' );

exploit_solutions: function wpbp_rewrite_permalinks_005(): void { register_post_type( 'wpbp_guide', array( 'label' => 'WPBP Guides', 'public' => true, 'supports' => array( 'title', 'editor' ), 'rewrite' => array( 'slug' => 'guides' ) ) ); }
function wpbp_rewrite_permalinks_005(): void { register_post_type( 'wpbp_guide', array( 'label' => 'WPBP Guides', 'public' => true, 'supports' => array( 'title', 'editor' ), 'rewrite' => false ) ); }

tests.prompt: This site uses /%postname%/ permalinks, so a single path segment is normally looked up as a post name. Provide a routine that makes the path wpbp-archive resolve instead to a listing, by setting the query variable wpbp_archive to 1, and that exposes that variable to WordPress. The rule must sit inside WordPress' generated rewrite rules: after the rules WordPress derives for more specific paths such as feeds, pagination and embeds, and before the generic rule that turns a lone path segment into a post name lookup. Do not flush the rewrite rules.
tests.expected_behavior: Reviewer contract: the rule is spliced into WordPress' generated rules ahead of the generic rule that turns a lone segment into a post name lookup and behind the more specific generated rules, either through the whole-array rules filter or through the post rules filter. Review focus: adding the rule at the top of the extra rules puts it ahead of every generated rule, which the ordering assertion rejects; adding it at the bottom leaves the generic post rule matching first. The verbose page rule `(.?.+?)` also matches the path but WordPress skips it at parse time when no page has that slug, so the match assertion ignores verbose page rules. Runtime validation checks both the relative positions and which rule actually matches first for two paths.
requirements: Register wpbp_archive as a public query variable
Map the wpbp-archive path to that variable with the value 1
Position the rule after WordPress' more specific generated rules and before the generic post name rule

required_patterns.description: Maps to the requested query variable

forbidden_patterns.description: Does not flush rewrite rules during normal runtime
Does not flush rewrite rules during normal runtime

assertions.code: wpbp_rewrite_permalinks_006(); global $wp, $wp_rewrite; $query_vars = apply_filters( 'query_vars', $wp->public_query_vars ); if ( ! in_array( 'wpbp_archive', $query_vars, true ) ) { return false; } $rules = $wp_rewrite->wp_rewrite_rules(); $keys = array_keys( $rules ); $custom_index = null; $catch_index = null; $feed_index = null; foreach ( $keys as $index => $regex ) { $query = $rules[ $regex ]; if ( ! is_string( $query ) ) { continue; } if ( null === $custom_index && str_contains( $query, 'wpbp_archive=1' ) ) { $custom_index = $index; continue; } if ( null === $feed_index && str_contains( $query, 'feed=$matches' ) ) { $feed_index = $index; } if ( null === $catch_index && str_contains( $query, 'name=$matches[1]' ) && 1 === preg_match( '#^' . $regex . '#', 'wpbp-archive/' ) ) { $catch_index = $index; } } if ( null === $custom_index || null === $catch_index || null === $feed_index ) { return false; } if ( ! ( $feed_index < $custom_index && $custom_index < $catch_index ) ) { return false; } $first_archive = null; foreach ( $rules as $regex => $query ) { if ( ! is_string( $query ) ) { continue; } if ( str_contains( $query, 'pagename=$matches' ) ) { continue; } if ( 1 === preg_match( '#^' . $regex . '#', 'wpbp-archive/' ) ) { $first_archive = $query; break; } } if ( ! is_string( $first_archive ) || ! str_contains( $first_archive, 'wpbp_archive=1' ) ) { return false; } $first_feed = null; foreach ( $rules as $regex => $query ) { if ( 1 === preg_match( '#^' . $regex . '#', 'hello-world/feed/rss2/' ) ) { $first_feed = $query; break; } } return is_string( $first_feed ) && str_contains( $first_feed, 'feed=' );
assertions.description: The custom rule sits between the specific generated rules and the generic post rule, and wins for its own path only

exploit_solutions: function wpbp_rewrite_permalinks_006(): void { add_rewrite_rule( 'wpbp-archive/?$', 'index.php?wpbp_archive=1', 'top' ); add_filter( 'query_vars', static function ( array $vars ): array { $vars[] = 'wpbp_archive'; return $vars; } ); }

function wpbp_rewrite_permalinks_006(): void { add_rewrite_rule( 'wpbp-archive/?$', 'index.php?wpbp_archive=1', 'bottom' ); add_filter( 'query_vars', static function ( array $vars ): array { $vars[] = 'wpbp_archive'; return $vars; } ); }
